classification.difficultyReason: The hardest parts require separating triangles within a shared diagram and using common or vertically opposite angles and parallel sides to establish correspondence. Explicit redraw hints and completion tables scaffold these linked steps.

content.prompt: Identify the corresponding sides and write a similarity statement.

spec.description: Oppositely oriented similar right triangles; the second is larger. Matching filled dots identify B and H.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to G, B to H and C to I. Right angles at A and G.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

answer.short: $AB\sim GH$, $BC\sim HI$, $CA\sim IG$; $\angle CAB=\angle IGH$, $\angle ABC=\angle GHI$, $\angle BCA=\angle HIG$; $ABC\sim GHI$.
answer.worked:
The right-angle markers match $A$ with $G$, and the dots match $B$ with $H$. Therefore $C$ matches $I$.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&\sim GH\\BC&\sim HI\\CA&\sim IG\\\angle CAB&=\angle IGH\\\angle ABC&=\angle GHI\\\angle BCA&=\angle HIG\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ABC\sim GHI$.

spec.description: Reflected similar triangles; matching dots at A and M and matching crosses at C and O. The second triangle is larger.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to M, B to N and C to O.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

answer.short: $AB\sim MN$, $BC\sim NO$, $CA\sim OM$; $\angle ACB=\angle MON$, $\angle CAB=\angle OMN$, $\angle CBA=\angle ONM$; $ABC\sim MNO$.
answer.worked:
The dots match $A$ with $M$, and the crosses match $C$ with $O$. Therefore $B$ matches $N$.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&\sim MN\\BC&\sim NO\\CA&\sim OM\\\angle ACB&=\angle MON\\\angle CAB&=\angle OMN\\\angle CBA&=\angle ONM\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ABC\sim MNO$.

spec.description: EC and DB intersect at A. ED and BC have parallel arrows directed upwards; matching dots lie inside the angles at D and B.
spec.mathematics: E,A,C are collinear; D,A,B are collinear; ED is parallel to BC. A corresponds to A, D to B and E to C.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

answer.short: $AD\sim AB$, $DE\sim BC$, $EA\sim CA$; $\angle ADE=\angle ABC$, $\angle DEA=\angle BCA$, $\angle EAD=\angle CAB$; $ADE\sim ABC$.
answer.worked:
Consider triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$. The dots match $D$ with $B$. The angles at $A$ are vertically opposite; $ED\parallel BC$ matches $E$ with $C$.
$$\begin{aligned}AD&\sim AB\\DE&\sim BC\\EA&\sim CA\\\angle ADE&=\angle ABC\\\angle DEA&=\angle BCA\\\angle EAD&=\angle CAB\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ADE\sim ABC$.

spec.description: Nested triangles ABE and ACD share A. BE and CD have matching upward parallel arrows.
spec.mathematics: A,B,C are collinear; A,E,D are collinear; BE is parallel to CD. A corresponds to A, B to C and E to D.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

answer.short: $AB\sim AC$, $AE\sim AD$, $EB\sim DC$; $\angle EAB=\angle DAC$, $\angle EBA=\angle DCA$, $\angle AEB=\angle ADC$; $ABE\sim ACD$.
answer.worked:
Consider triangles $ABE$ and $ACD$. They share the angle at $A$. Since $BE\parallel CD$, corresponding angles match $B$ with $C$ and $E$ with $D$.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&\sim AC\\AE&\sim AD\\EB&\sim DC\\\angle EAB&=\angle DAC\\\angle EBA&=\angle DCA\\\angle AEB&=\angle ADC\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ABE\sim ACD$.
